docs.title: Modern HomingCast
docs.text: The modern version of HomingCast uses the core system of SwiftCast as a foundation, but still focuses specifically on homing projectile functionality

docs.title: Callbacks
docs.text:
Callbacks are functions defined within settings that allow you to define custom behavior of a projectile when certain events occur

Each callback is marked with

  • r for direct read permission
  • w for direct write permission

There are currently 8 callbacks present

docs.title: OnStep [rw]
docs.text:
Fires every time the projectile steps even if the velocity is 0

OnStep = function(projectile: Projectile, deltaTime: number): nil

docs.title: OnPositionChange [rw]
docs.text:
Fires every time the projectile steps except when the velocity is 0

OnPositionChange = function(projectile: Projectile, newPosition: Vector3, oldPosition: Vector3): nil

docs.title: OnDestroy [rw]
docs.text:
Fires when the projectile is destroyed

OnDestroy = function(projectile: Projectile, reason: string | "MaxTime" | "MaxDistance" | "Hit"): nil

docs.title: OnHit [rw]
docs.text:
Fires when the projectile hits something

OnHit = function(projectile: Projectile, result: RaycastResult, hasPierced: boolean): nil

docs.title: OnTargetLost [rw]
docs.text:
Fires when the projectile exceeds MaxTrackAngle

OnTargetLost = function(projectile: Projectile, target: Vector3 | BasePart): nil

Note

After OnTargetLost is fired, the target is set to nil

docs.title: OnCheckpointReached [rw]
docs.text:
Fires when the checkpoint inside of trajectory is reached

OnCheckpointReached = function(projectile: Projectile, checkpoint: string): nil

Note

After OnCheckpointReached is fired, the checkpoint is set to nil

docs.title: PostTransform [r]
docs.text:
Due to the way Motor6D.Transform works we made a PostTransform callback which is called right after .Transform is applied for the first time. Otherwise the CFrame of the cosmetic part will appear as origin

PostTransform = function(projectile: Projectile): nil

docs.title: PostTransformSafe [r]
docs.text:
This is the 2nd PostTransform. Basically the second time .Transform is applied. This is helpful to safely toggle vfx on or make parts visible to hide the pre .Transform phase

PostTransformSafe = function(projectile: Projectile): nil

docs.title: UseProtectedCalls (boolean)
docs.text:
Uses protected calls for event callbacks

Default value is true

docs.title: StartOnRequire (boolean)
docs.text:
Starts the simulation on require

Default value is true

docs.title: MovementMethod ("BulkMoveTo" | "Transform")
docs.text:
Switches between BulkMoveTo and Transform movement methods

Default value is false

docs.title: RaySearchOffset (number)
docs.text:
The offset ray adds to the raycast position to search for the next hit

Default value is 0.001

docs.title: What is Custom Trajectory?
docs.text: Custom Trajectory is a property called Trajectory, which makes the projectile follow a predefined path

docs.title: How do I get this Trajectory?
docs.text: I created a plugin to simplify this process for you. Here is the plugin.

docs.title: How to use this Plugin?
docs.text:
Here are all the controls:

  • Double-click to create a new point. (These points are draggable.)

Reminder!

Since these points use UI Drag Detectors, you need to enable the beta feature in Roblox Studio called UI Drag Detectors

  • Press E on a point to change its state

What is State?

Each point currently has two states:

  • Free
  • Locked on Y-axis

If a point is locked on the Y-axis, its height won't be affected by the start position of the cast or the target's position. The Free state is the standard state, allowing height to change during flight

  • Use the mouse wheel to adjust the maximum height
  • Press G on a point to create a checkpoint

What is a Checkpoint?

A checkpoint contains a name. When the projectile reaches this point, it will fire the CheckpointReached callback.

docs.title: Saving and using the Trajectory
docs.text:
Once you've created the points, press the Save button. This will generate a script in ReplicatedStorage containing the trajectory table. Copy and paste this table into the Trajectory property

Example

Properties.Trajectory = {
    {Yscale = 0.3, Xscale = 0.12220414727926254, State = "Free", MaxHeight = 150},
    {Yscale = 0.6, Xscale = 0.310281366109848, State = "Free", MaxHeight = 150},
    {Yscale = 0.6, Xscale = 0.903989744186401, State = "Free", CheckPoint = "Above", MaxHeight = 150},
}

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
There're 2 modes:

  • Trajectory - To create a custom trajectory curve (default)
  • AoA - To create yaw / pitch angle of attack tables

To change the mode, click Mode button

docs.title: Physics
docs.text: Physics settings are now passed as a third parameter of HomingCast.SpawnProjectile/HomingCast.CreateProjectile methods as a table structure

docs.title: Physics properties allow you to simulate realisitic physics
docs.text:
How does this physics work?

This physics is based on missile's physics

Beware!

If you use physics, do not set physics properties to extremely high values as it can lead to jittering

Everything must be balanced

Each setting is marked with

  • r for direct read permission
  • w for direct write permission

docs.title: Mass [rw] (number)
docs.text:
Mass of the projectile

errors if omitted

Remember

Gravity value must be always negative when passed

docs.title: Gravity [rw] (number)
docs.text:
Gravity of the projectile

Default value is -9.81 if omitted

docs.title: LiftPower [rw] (number)
docs.text:
This is a constant for the lift coefficient. Determines aerodynamic capabilities of the projectile for pitch

errors if omitted

docs.title: YawPower [rw] (number)
docs.text:
This is a constant for the yaw coefficient. Determines aerodynamic capabilities of the projectile for yaw

errors if omitted

docs.title: DragCoefficient [rw] (number)
docs.text:
Determines the resistance of the projectile in a fluid environment

errors if omitted

docs.title: InducedDragYaw [rw] (number)
docs.text:
Determines the resistance of the projectile in a fluid environment when rotating on the yaw axis

errors if omitted

docs.title: InducedDragPitch [rw] (number)
docs.text:
Determines the resistance of the projectile in a fluid environment when rotating on the pitch axis

errors if omitted

docs.title: ThrustPower [rw] (number)
docs.text:
Sets the force which constantly pushes the projectile in its look direction

errors if omitted

docs.title: PitchAoA [rw] ({Value: number, AoA: number})
docs.text:
This is a list which determines the lift coefficient at some angle of attack

errors if omitted

Example

PhysicsProperties.PitchAoA = {
    {["Value"] = -0.12,["AoA"] = -65},
    {["Value"] = -1,["AoA"] = -25},
    {["Value"] = 0,["AoA"] = 0},
    {["Value"] = 1,["AoA"] = 25},
    {["Value"] = 0.12,["AoA"] = 65}
}

Recommendations

Value should be from [-1 to 1]. But you can set to any value you want

How do I get this table?

Use my plugin for this and change the mode to AoA

Read about it here

docs.title: YawAoA [rw] ({Value: number, AoA: number})
docs.text:
This is a list which determines the yaw coefficient at some angle of attack yaw

errors if omitted

Example

PhysicsProperties.YawAoA = {
    {["Value"] = -0.12,["AoA"] = -65},
    {["Value"] = -1,["AoA"] = -25},
    {["Value"] = 0,["AoA"] = 0},
    {["Value"] = 1,["AoA"] = 25},
    {["Value"] = 0.12,["AoA"] = 65}
}

Recommendations

Value should be from [-1 to 1]. But you can set to any value you want

How do I get this table?

Use my plugin for this and change the mode to AoA

Read about it here

Remember

The Value will be smoothed from one to another value based on given angle of attack (pitch / yaw)

docs.title: G_Limit [rw] (number)
docs.text:
G limit of the projectile

errors if omitted

docs.title: Direction [rw] (Vector3)
docs.text:
Determines at what direction the projectile is rotated after launch

errors if omitted

docs.title: AdditionalForces [rw] (Vector3)
docs.text:
Additional force which will effect on the cast constantly

Default value is Vector3.zero if omitted

docs.title: Raycast function
docs.text:
In order to use the raycast function, access it as HomingCast.RaycastFunctions.YOUR_RAYCAST_FUNCTION and put it inside of parameters under RaycastFunction key

There are currently 4 types of raycast functions present

docs.title: Raycast (Default)
docs.text: Uses Raycast to detect the hits

docs.title: BlockCast
docs.text: Uses Blockcast to detect the hits

docs.title: Spherecast
docs.text: Uses Spherecast to detect the hits

docs.title: Shapecast
docs.text: Uses Shapecast to detect the hits

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings are now passed as a first parameter of HomingCast.SpawnProjectile/HomingCast.CreateProjectile methods as a table structure

Example

local HomingCast = require(.../HomingCast)

HomingCast.SpawnProjectile({YOUR SETTINGS})

How do I reuse common settings?

In order to reuse common properties and don't pass the table everytime you can use HomingCast.ProjetileSettings.new({YOUR COMMON SETTINGS})

And pass it as the second parameter of HomingCast.SpawnProjectile/HomingCast.CreateProjectile methods

Settings can be accessed inside of projectile and changed/read during the runtime

Each setting is marked with

  • r for direct read permission
  • w for direct write permission
  • b for built-in function to edit

There are a lot of settings and they all are listed here!

docs.title: MaxFlyDistance [rw] (number)
docs.text:
If the projectile covers this distance, it will be terminated

Terminated

This will fire OnDestroy callback: 

OnDestroy = function(projectile: Projectile, reason: string)
The Reason will be "MaxDistance"

Default value is math.huge if omitted

docs.title: MaxFlyTime [rw] (number)
docs.text:
If the projectile flies longer than this value, it will be terminated

Terminated

This will fire OnDestroy callback: 

OnDestroy = function(projectile: Projectile, reason: string)
The Reason will be "MaxTime"

Default value is math.huge if omitted

docs.title: MaxPiercesPerStep [rw] (number)
docs.text:
Defines how many times projectile can pierce the objects before continuing its movement

Default value is 1 if omitted

docs.title: MaxTrackAngle [rb] (number)
docs.text:
If the target moves outside this angle, the projectile will lose track of it and set the target to nil

Value must be given in degrees

Default value is 180 if omitted

If the value is 180 it means that projectile will never lose its target

Target lost

This will fire OnTargetLost callback: 

OnTargetLost = function(projectile: Projectile, target: Vector3 | BasePart)

Note

In order to properly set the value of this property you can use: HomingCast.SetMaxTrackAngle(projectile: Projectile, angle: number)

Can be set manually by following this formula math.clamp(math.cos(math.rad(angle)), -1, 1) where angle is your desired value in degrees

docs.title: Prediction [rw] (boolean)
docs.text:
Defines if the projectile tries to predict the future position of the given target based on its velocity and position using proportional navigation (PN)

Default value is false if omitted

docs.title: Target [rb] (Model | BasePart | Vector3 | nil)
docs.text:
The target to which the projectile will try to rotate towards

Default value is nil if omitted

If the value is nil the projectile will continue its movement towards the direction of the projectile's velocity

Note

In order to properly set the value of this property you can use: HomingCast.SetTarget(projectile: Projectile, target: Model | BasePart | Vector3 | nil)

Remember

The projectile's target can be set to nil automatically if the projectile exceeded MaxTrackAngle

docs.title: Offset [rw] (Vector3)
docs.text:
The offset which is applied to target's position

Can be a funtion in order to give unique behaviour for the projectile

Offset = function(projectile: Projectile, deltaTime: number, targetPosition: Vector3, targetVelocity: Vector3): Vector3

Default value is Vector3.zero if omitted

docs.title: RotationSpeed [rb] (number)
docs.text:
Defines the speed at which the projectile turns

Default value is 30 if omitted

Note

In order to properly set the value of this property you can use: HomingCast.SetRotationSpeed(projectile: Projectile, angle: number)

Can be set manually by following this formula math.rad(angle) where angle is your desired value in degrees

docs.title: RaycastParams [rw] (RaycastParams)
docs.text:
Defines the RaycastParams for the cast

Default value is nil if omitted

docs.title: Trajectory [rw] ({TrajectoryNode})
docs.text:
The projectile will attempt to follow the given trajectory

For more information, see Custom Trajectories

Default value is nil if omitted

docs.title: RaycastFunction [rw] (RaycastFunction)
docs.text:
Defines which type of cast will be used to detect the hit of the projectile

For more information, see Raycast Functions

Default value is Default (Raycast) if omitted

docs.title: ProjectilePart [rb] (BasePart)
docs.text:
The projectile's cosmetic part

Default value is nil if omitted

Note

In order to properly set the value of this property you can use: HomingCast.SetProjectilePart(projectile: Projectile, basePart: BasePart?)

docs.title: ProjectilePartRotation [rw] (CFrame)
docs.text:
The projectile's part's rotation

Default value is CFrame.identity if omitted and no projectile part

docs.title: CanPierce [rw] (boolean)
docs.text:
The value which defines if the projectile can pierce the object and continue its movement

Can be a funtion in order to give unique behaviour for the projectile

CanPierce = function(projectile: Projectile, result: RaycastResult): boolean

Default value is false if omitted

Note

If CanPierce returns true, it will fire OnHit callback

OnHit = function(projectile: Projectile, result: RaycastResult, hasPierced: boolean)

The hasPierced in this specific case will be false

docs.title: Userdata [rw] (any)
docs.text:
User's custom data

Default value is nil if omitted

docs.title: BlockcastSize [rw] (number)
docs.text:
The value which is used for specific type of cast

Default value is nil if omitted

Can cause an warning if nil and the raycast function is used

docs.title: SpherecastRadius [rw] (number)
docs.text:
The value which is used for specific type of cast

Default value is nil if omitted

Can cause an warning if nil and the raycast function is used

docs.title: ShapecastPart [rw] (BasePart)
docs.text:
The value which is used for specific type of cast

Default value is nil if omitted

Can cause an warning if nil and the raycast function is used

docs.title: States
docs.text:
There are states inside of projectile raw table

Each state is marked with

  • r for direct read permission
  • w for direct write permission

docs.title: Position [rw] (number)
docs.text: Current projectile's position

docs.title: Velocity [rw] (number)
docs.text: Current projectile's velocity

docs.text: How much time elapsed after the projectile was created

docs.title: Guide
docs.text:
Legacy version

This is the legacy version of HomingCast and is not recommended for new projects

It is still maintained and may receive updates if useful features or improvements are suggested

For new projects, use the modern version of HomingCast

docs.title: HomingCast
docs.text:
HomingCast is a module that allows you to create dynamic, real-time simulated homing projectiles without relying on Roblox physics

For example, it can be used for missiles, spells, or homing bullets

Download: HomingCast

It is similar to FastCast, which is designed to simulate projectile drop physics. However, HomingCast focuses on creating homing projectiles without using Roblox physics

Recommendation

FastCast is not recommended for new projects

A more modern alternative is SwiftCast.

docs.title: What is Caster?
docs.text: This page describes what the Caster

docs.title: How to get Caster
docs.text:
To get Caster, you first need to require the module:

local HomingCast = require(.../HomingCast)

Then, create the Caster:

local Caster = HomingCast.new()

Remember!

The Caster must be created only once, as it serves as the base for all casts

docs.title: What is Caster?
docs.text:
Caster is used to start the simulation of a cast

Caster:Fire(StartPosition: Vector3, StartDirection: Vector3, Speed: number | Vector3, Target: Model | BasePart | Vector3, Properties, PhysicsProperties?)

How to get Properties?

To get Properties, use:

local Properties: {} = HomingCast.NewProperties()

Read more about Properties.

The Caster:Fire function returns an InfoCast

Beware

If you use physics simulation, speed parameter will become not a constant speed, but an impulse

If Speed parameter is number then impluse will be applied in StartDirection

docs.title: PositionChanged
docs.text:
PositionChanged(InfoCast, Position: Vector3, Direction: Vector3, Distance: number, Target: Vector3 | BasePart, CosmeticBullet: any?, UserData: {})

This signal fires every time the Caster moves

Useful Tip!

If you want your projectile to follow the path and align with the flight direction, use this code:

Caster.PositionChanged:Connect(function(...) 
    if CosmeticBullet then
        local BulletSize = CosmeticBullet.Size.Z / 2
        local Offset = CFrame.new(0, 0, -(Distance - BulletSize))
        CosmeticBullet.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(Position, Position + Direction):ToWorldSpace(Offset)
    end
end)

docs.title: RayHit
docs.text:
RayHit(InfoCast, RayCastResult: RaycastResult, Direction: Vector3, CosmeticBullet: any?, UserData: {})

This signal fires when the Caster hits something

docs.title: Terminated
docs.text:
Terminated(InfoCast, Reason: string, CosmeticBullet: BasePart?, UserData: {})

This signal fires when the Caster terminates due to exceeding the maximum flight distance, exceeding maximum flight time, or being manually terminated

What is Reason?

The Reason parameter indicates why the cast was terminated. Possible values:

  • Custom Reason - The reason that was defined in TerminateCast method
  • Self - The cast was terminated manually
  • MaxDistance - The cast exceeded the maximum flight distance
  • MaxFlyTime - The cast exceeded the maximum flight time

docs.title: TargetLost
docs.text:
TargetLost(InfoCast, LostTarget: Vector3 | BasePart, Position: Vector3, Direction: Vector3, CosmeticBullet: any?, UserData: {})

This signal fires when the Caster loses its target

docs.title: CheckpointReached
docs.text:
CheckpointReached(InfoCast, CheckpointName: string, Position: Vector3, Direction: Vector3, CosmeticBulletTemplate: any?, UserData: {})

This signal fires when the Caster reaches a point in the trajectory

Custom Trajectory

More information about Custom Trajectories.

docs.title: What is InfoCast?
docs.text: InfoCast is a modified version of Caster. It contains all properties, the current position, direction, reference to the Caster, etc.

docs.title: Where do I get InfoCast?
docs.text:
InfoCast is returned in all 5 signals. Read more about it here.

Additionally, when you start a simulation using:

local InfoCast = Caster:Fire(...)

You will receive an InfoCast.

docs.title: Retrieving all active InfoCast
docs.text:
You can retrieve all currently simulated InfoCast using the function HomingCast.GetAllInfoCast():

local HomingCast = require(.../HomingCast)

local PreActiveInfoCasts, PostActiveInfoCasts = HomingCast.GetAllInfoCast()

Returns 2 tables that contain all PreActiveInfoCasts and all PostActiveInfoCasts (PreSimulation and PostSimulation)

docs.title: This feature was removed in update 1.7
docs.text:
To enable this feature, do the following:

local HomingCast = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.HomingCast)

HomingCast.AmountOfActors = 10
HomingCast.PositionSendDelay = 0.1

local caster = HomingCast.new()

What is PositionSendDelay?

PositionSendDelay determines how often the PositionChanged signal is fired

The smaller the PositionSendDelay is, the fewer projectiles you can handle

Note!

AmountOfActors and PositionSendDelay must be set before creating a new caster!

Parallel mode can only be used on server side!

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
I don't recommend using this feature, as it won’t allow significantly more projectiles at once, and the following features are not available in parallel mode:

1) All methods are unavailable

2) Visualization is unavailable

3) Offset, Scaler, CosmeticBulletTemplate and SimulateBeforePhysics properties are unavailable

Additionally, to use signals, you must add .Event due to the use of BindableEvents

Example

caster.PositionChanged.Event:Connect()

docs.title: Physics properties allow you to simulate realisitic physics
docs.text:
To access these properties, you first need to require the module:

local HomingCast = require(.../HomingCast)

Then, create the properties:

local PhysicsProperties: {} = HomingCast.NewPhysicsProperties()

How does this physics work?

This physics is based on missile's physics

Beware!

If you use physics, do not set physics properties to extremely high values as it can lead to jittering

Everything must be balanced

docs.title: PitchAoA
docs.text:
PhysicsProperties.PitchAoA :: {}
This is a list which determines the lift coefficient at some angle of attack

Example

PhysicsProperties.PitchAoA = {
    {["Value"] = -0.12,["AoA"] = -65},
    {["Value"] = -1,["AoA"] = -25},
    {["Value"] = 0,["AoA"] = 0},
    {["Value"] = 1,["AoA"] = 25},
    {["Value"] = 0.12,["AoA"] = 65}
}

Recommendations

Value should be from [-1 to 1]. But you can set to any value you want

How do I get this table?

Use my plugin for this and change the mode to AoA

Read about it here

docs.title: YawAoA
docs.text:
PhysicsProperties.YawAoA :: {}
This is a list which determines the yaw coefficient at some angle of attack yaw

Example

PhysicsProperties.YawAoA = {
    {["Value"] = -0.12,["AoA"] = -65},
    {["Value"] = -1,["AoA"] = -25},
    {["Value"] = 0,["AoA"] = 0},
    {["Value"] = 1,["AoA"] = 25},
    {["Value"] = 0.12,["AoA"] = 65}
}

Recommendations

Value should be from [-1 to 1]. But you can set to any value you want

How do I get this table?

Use my plugin for this and change the mode to AoA

Read about it here

Remember

The Value will be smoothed from one to another value based on given angle of attack (pitch / yaw)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
To access properties, you first need to require the module:

local HomingCast = require(.../HomingCast)

Then, create the properties:

local Properties: {} = HomingCast.NewProperties()

Can I create more Properties?

Yes, you can! This can be useful for different scenarios. For example, if your spell hits something and creates sub-spells, you can create additional properties to give them different behaviors

docs.title: There are a lot of properties and they all are listed here!
MaxDistance
docs.text:
Properties.MaxDistance :: number
If the cast covers this distance, it will be terminated

Terminated!

This will fire: 

Caster.Terminated(InfoCast, Reason: string, CosmeticBullet: BasePart?, UserData: {})
The Reason will be "MaxDistance"

docs.title: MaxFlyTime
docs.text:
Properties.MaxFlyTime :: number
If the cast flies longer than this value, it will be terminated

Terminated!

This will fire: 

Caster.Terminated(InfoCast, Reason: string, CosmeticBullet: BasePart?, UserData: {})
The Reason will be "MaxFlyTime"

docs.text:
Properties.RaysPerMove :: number
Determines how many raycasts will be fired in one move.

Performance Warning!

Setting this value too high (e.g., 20 or more) can cause significant lag

Recommended values range from 1 to 5

docs.text:
Properties.Prediction :: boolean
If false, target prediction is disabled. If true then module will predict the target's future position based on its velocity and position

docs.title: Trajectory
docs.text:
Properties.Trajectory :: {}?
If not nil, the projectile will attempt to follow the given trajectory. (Optional)

For more information, see Custom Trajectories.

Example

Properties.Trajectory = {
    {Yscale = 0.3, Xscale = 0.12220414727926254, State = "Free", MaxHeight = 150},
    {Yscale = 0.6, Xscale = 0.310281366109848, State = "Free", MaxHeight = 150},
    {Yscale = 0.6, Xscale = 0.903989744186401, State = "Free", CheckPoint = "Above", MaxHeight = 150},
}

docs.title: HighPrecision
docs.text:
Properties.HighPrecision :: number
If this value is greater than 0 (e.g., 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, ..., 1), the module will perform a secondary accuracy check after a low-fidelity raycast detects a hit. This value determines how precise the recalculations will be. (Optional)

Performance Warning!

Setting this value to extreme small numbers (e.g., 0.01 or smaller) can cause significant lag

Recommended values range from 0.1

docs.title: Offset
docs.text:
Properties.Offset :: ((TotalTime: number, DeltaTime: number, TargetPosition: Vector3, CurrentPosition: Vector3) -> (Vector3))?
This function affects the target's position

Example

Properties.Offset = function(TotalTime, DeltaTime, TargetPosition, CurrentPosition)
    return Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
end
The projectile will fly above the target's actual position

How does Offset work?

TargetPosition += Offset(TotalTime, DeltaTime, TargetPosition, CurrentPosition)

docs.title: Scaler
docs.text:
Properties.Scaler :: ((TotalTime: number, DeltaTime: number, TargetPosition: Vector3, CurrentPosition: Vector3) -> (Vector3 | number))?
This function affects the target's position

How does Scaler work?

TargetPosition *= Scaler(TotalTime, DeltaTime, TargetPosition, CurrentPosition)

Remember!

First, the target's position will be scaled, and then an offset will be applied 

TargetPosition = TargetPosition * Scaler(...) + Offset(...)
